(a) adaptive time and power allocation is a viable approach for spectrum sharing between primary and secondary systems in cognitive radio broadcast channels; (b) spectrum sensing information at the secondary base-station is a useful tool in the resource management; (c) quantized spectrum sensing information is a viable alternative to full soft-sensing, which results in lower system complexity; (d) spectrum-aware sensors can improve the performance of spectrum sharing systems.

(a) adaptive time-sharing and power control policies are optimal for resource management in spectrum-sharing CR BC; (b) the optimal time-sharing and transmit power policies are independent of the secondary fading channel gains; (c) the achievable capacity of the spectrum-sharing BC is a non-decreasing and concave function of the sensing threshold; and, (d) the optimal time sharing and transmit power policies for a spectrum-sharing BC are independent of the primary activity level.
